section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "a locked garden" is like betrothal, where mitzvos create a surrounding separation from desires (like betrothal), preparing a vessel to receive the inner drawing of Torah (like marriage).
section.t: And this will be understood based on what is said in the maamar,
that "a locked garden" is like the concept of betrothal.
And he explains this based on the known [teaching]
regarding the concept of "Sanctify us with Your commandments and give our portion in Your Torah,"
that "Sanctify us with Your commandments" is from the term betrothal,
for the concept of betrothal is designation,
that the woman who is betrothed is designated and set apart for her husband, and through this she is forbidden to all the world,
and "give our portion in Your Torah" is the concept of marriage,
a drawing down into the innerness,
to the point that the person absorbs the drawing down,
to the point that it becomes "our portion"
(of Israel).
And this is "Sanctify us with Your commandments and give our portion in Your Torah,"
that the drawing down through the mitzvos is in the aspect of surrounding [light],
and its effect upon the person who performs the mitzvah is
(primarily)
that he be separated from desires and from all evil attributes,
similar to betrothal,
for this that the woman is betrothed to her husband is
(primarily)
this that she is forbidden to all the world.
And through this he becomes a vessel to absorb the light of Torah,
"and Your Torah within my innards,"
marriage.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section adds that the analogy of mitzvos and Torah to betrothal and marriage is in two aspects: the manner of drawing down (surrounding vs. internal) and the quality of the drawing itself (Torah's drawing is more elevated and intrinsic).
section.t: And one may add,
that the comparison of mitzvos and Torah to betrothal and marriage is in two matters.
In the manner of the drawing down,
that the drawing down of the mitzvos upon the person who performs the mitzvah is in the aspect of surrounding [light]
(betrothal)
and the drawing down of Torah upon the person who engages in Torah is in the innerness
(marriage)
as above.
And also in the drawing down itself.
For the drawing down of Torah is a more elevated and inner drawing down than the drawing down of mitzvos
[to the point that the drawing down of mitzvos is the aspect of hind-parts relative to the drawing down of Torah],
and therefore,
the drawing down of Torah is similar to the drawing down of the drop
(marriage)
which is an intrinsic drawing down.
And it may be said,
that also this concept is hinted at in "and give our portion in Your Torah."
For in the language "our portion" there are two matters.
That the Torah becomes our portion of Israel
(as above),
and that it is a portion of the Holy One, blessed be He,
for when you grasp a part of the essence, you grasp all of it.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Sanctify us with Your commandments" is a preparation for "give our portion in Your Torah," analogous to the mitzvos given before the Exodus and at Marah as preparations for the Giving of the Torah.
section.t: And one may add,
that this that "Sanctify us with Your commandments" is a preface to "give our portion in Your Torah,"
is one of the reasons that before the Exodus from Egypt the portion of HaChodesh was said,
which contains several mitzvos
[that are practiced for generations and are counted among the 613 mitzvos],
for with the Exodus from Egypt the concept of the Giving of the Torah began,
and therefore before the Exodus from Egypt they were commanded in several mitzvos,
which was a preface to the concept of the Giving of the Torah that began with the Exodus from Egypt.
And after this they were commanded ten mitzvos at Marah
which was a preparation for the actual Giving of the Torah.
And more generally it may be said,
that this that the Torah begins with Bereishis because of "the strength
of His works He declared to His people, to give them the inheritance of the nations"
is in the manner of the preface of the performance of mitzvos to Torah,
for most of the mitzvos are dependent on the Land
(the inheritance of the nations).
